variants.candidate: What you keep inside does not count as finished. Make one thing a week that someone else can hold. Say the opinion you have been sitting on to one person. Show a child or a friend something you know how to do. Write one line down before bed.
variants.original: Enthusiasm fades, structure remembers. After every burst of inspiration, spend one hour making it hold: a document, a recipe, a repeatable plan. Host the gathering twice and it becomes tradition. Write down the thing you keep explaining.

variants.candidate: You give out faster than you take in, and running on your own fuel feels like energy until it runs out. Read one long book a chapter at a time. Sit with a question overnight before you answer it. Ask someone older how they did it and listen past the first sentence. Nap before the next idea.
variants.original: Brilliance is mostly patience with good storage. Keep one slow project that grows monthly, a course, a craft, a language, and refuse to rush it. Finish books. Choose one person to learn from properly this year and stay teachable.

variants.candidate: You do your best work with a date on it and someone waiting at the other end. Give each big plan a finish line before you start it. Once a month, hand a decision to someone whose call you will keep. Tell one person your deadline. Set a stop time before you begin.
variants.original: Discipline, for you, is imported, so import it well. Sleep on anything irreversible. Keep a reviewer you cannot charm and show them everything big. Put a cool number on every hot plan before saying yes.

variants.candidate: You treat rest as a loss and company as a crutch. Refuel on purpose: sleep before the second wind arrives. Eat with a peer once a week and let them pay. Ask one person for help on a job you usually do alone. Sit still for ten minutes a day.
variants.original: A light that never recharges becomes an act. Schedule recovery like meetings: real breaks between social blocks, daylight before screens, one morning a week with no one to perform for. Cancel something small today and feel what returns.

variants.candidate: Your drive outruns the places you have to put it, and an opening you only look at becomes weight. Pick one venture and give it a finish date. Move a fixed sum into savings each month before you spend the rest. Tell the man who raised you one thing you built this year. Finish one small thing before bed.
variants.original: Difficulty is your natural price filter, so use it openly. Take the assignment everyone else avoids. Price your work higher than feels comfortable and let the discomfort season. Once a year, pick one skill hard enough to embarrass you for months.
